The company built on breakthroughs. ​
Join us.​
Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible.  ​
How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​
​At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​
​Come break through with us.
Corning's Manufacturing, Technology and Engineering division (MTE) is recognized as the leader in engineering excellence & innovative manufacturing technologies by providing diverse skills to Corning’s existing & emerging businesses.
We anticipate & provide timely, valued, leading edge manufacturing technologies and engineering expertise.  We partner with Corning’s businesses and the Science & Technology division. Together we create and sustain Corning’s manufacturing as a differential advantage.
Role Purpose
Corning is seeking a motivated and technically curious Controls Engineering Intern to support the development and expansion of the Digital Factory Lab, an advanced automation training and demonstration platform. This internship offers hands-on experience with modern manufacturing technologies, including industrial robotics, machine vision, intelligent conveyance systems, programmable control systems, industrial networking, and automated material handling.
The Digital Factory Lab is designed not only as a hands-on automation training platform, but also as a testbed for emerging digital manufacturing concepts, including the collection and utilization of manufacturing data to support future artificial intelligence and intelligent automation applications.
As a member of the engineering team, you will work alongside experienced controls and automation engineers to help design, build, program, test, document, and demonstrate a state-of-the-art training platform used to teach advanced manufacturing concepts and emerging automation technologies.
Program Perks:
Competitive salaries
Assistance with housing and travel
Meaningful project and final project presentation
Intern Activities:
Social and networking opportunities
Weekly tech talks
Community involvement
Key Responsibilities
Support the assembly, maintenance, and organization of the Digital Factory Lab.
Assist with the mechanical integration of conveyors, sensors, robotics, vision systems, and automation hardware.
Wire sensors, actuators, control panels, and communication devices under engineering supervision.
Participate in programming and troubleshooting programmable controllers, robotic systems, operator interfaces, and industrial networks.
Design and fabricate custom components, fixtures, and sensor-mounting solutions using CAD and additive manufacturing technologies.
Learn the safe operation and application of robotic systems, automated conveyance equipment, and industrial machinery.
Collaborate with project leaders and engineers to meet project milestones and stage-gate objectives.
Document engineering activities, test results, lessons learned, and system configurations.
Participate in projects that collect, contextualize, visualize, and analyze manufacturing data to support future applications of artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, digital twins, and intelligent automation.
Contribute to the development of training materials, laboratory exercises, and technical demonstrations.
Assist with presentations and demonstrations for engineering teams, visitors, and leadership.
Present project accomplishments and technical learnings at the conclusion of the internship.
Experiences/Education - Required
Pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Robotics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Demonstrated technical curiosity and a desire to learn.
Basic electrical and mechanical aptitude.
Basic programming experience in any language.
Strong organizational, communication, and teamwork skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a laboratory environment.
Experiences/Education - Desired
Experience with robotics projects, engineering clubs, maker activities, or laboratory research.
Exposure to control systems, automation, embedded systems, or industrial equipment.
Familiarity with CAD software, 3D printing, or mechanical design.
Participation in robotics competitions, capstone projects, or similar hands-on engineering activities.
Interest in advanced manufacturing, automation, digital transformation, and emerging industrial technologies.
Why Join Us?
This internship provides a unique opportunity to work on a highly visible automation platform that integrates robotics, vision, controls, networking, and advanced manufacturing technologies into a single learning environment. The platform is also being developed as a foundation for future data-driven manufacturing applications, enabling exploration of artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, digital twins, and intelligent decision-support technologies within industrial environments. Interns will gain practical engineering experience, work alongside experienced professionals, and contribute directly to future training and demonstration capabilities across Corning. Build systems that generate the manufacturing data, connectivity, and operational context needed for AI-driven manufacturing solutions.
This position does not support immigration sponsorship.
​The range for this position is $1,635.00 - $3,185.00 biweekly.  Starting pay for the successful applicant is prescribed based on geographic location, nature of position, and year in school.
